chapter: Brass bands, Buddy Petit and horns
title: Buddy borrowing horns and an unclear closing fragment
summary: Buddy borrowed horns from everyone; a rambling story of a packed job, then fragmentary brawl and unrelated closing talk.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition

blocks.x: Did Buddy ever have his own horn? He had it sometimes. Once in a while, huh?

Yeah. I don't know, he used to farm up there. He said, he had to borrow horns from everybody. He's lucky to get them. So he, he, I learned, I wasn't going to horn for him. I learned to him. And, uh, he was bringing back, uh, on Monday, next Monday. That, that, that wasn't my arm at all. I brought it off. I just brought the lens to bless the buzz like I didn't ever let the buzz get. And, uh, place, place was packed. Pack and jam with, with, with people. Copper is all too. And, uh, I, I, I knocked off at, uh, one o'clock while I was there. Uh, we, we, we got all the food ones. Pack and people. Tied and all. They put a copper, copper through. And, uh, I take some gold, gold, uh, butter house. We didn't live before from there. And, uh, I'm not going to pick up my horn while I'm there. I go there and pick it up. And, uh, my father said, I said, what ain't ya? What ain't ya? I go up by that. You got a copper, you know? I told you, he ain't broke up here and he stood by the pick-up like now. I said, you sure you got it? He said, yeah. That time, he said, you know, you should get hot. What are you to do? I said, long before I beat up around that quick, I got a buzz. He's blocked from there. I said, I got a young, I got a young, I got a young, I got a young, I got a, all the pack. But it's time I said, my home is a blunt. I said, how about it? He said, how about it? He said, how about it? He said, how about it? How about it? How about it? Keep going. And, uh, I said, about two numbers. And, uh, I said, I don't know where I'm going. The fuck? He said, uh, I've been around the last one. Eh? It won't be, it ain't, uh, trouble. You know, if I'm not going to knock him off. I said, listen, brother, I'm going to be stupid. I said, you ain't going to knock me up. You ain't going to get no play, ain't going to get no horn. I said, I'm going to take the horn while I'm playing, while I'm leaving. And I ain't going to stop. And, uh, you see, they had the clan there. I said, the clan there too good. Cause every time I go by your law, my wife said, you ain't coming, ain't that good. I ain't do that. It was a lot. And, uh, I said, look, look, I'll be in front of the Colorado, all on the, all on the different thing, but I can see the case. I'm going to look at it. I'll take it. And, uh, let's see. Be there, right? He'd be there somewhere too. And, uh, so then, one day, I, I, I, I came in there, right, right behind him. I go inside, I see him. Uh, uh, I was from the outside. I left the outside, I left the outside, I left behind, but, you know, there is this, you see. But, we don't get a man, you know, you're right down now.

I was freaking drunk, half drunk and spent all the money on the way. I knew he got nothing. I said, I don't want the arms. I got a good test. That's why I was like, I stepped on the table and pushed face. He was trying like he was on the table. He took a big dish, a big pan, a big old lousey and he killed that boy. I mean, bang! I was drunk again. He couldn't work. He got up and he was running outside. I said, oh, you're not hearing like that. I said, oh, you're not hearing like that.

Yeah, down the coast. He came from down the Beauderous down there. That's why he come. Yeah. We met her. She said, I said, how did that call? She told us her name. She was asking me. I sat down in the neighborhood and asked me if I know so and so. I said, I might know. She said, you got a bottom in town and two places. I said, yeah. I said, what's his name? She told me. And I was saying I didn't know. She told me the name. I thought they called him . Lipposian.
